answer: Each agent should earn influence only by completing tasks that other agents independently verify, with rewards released after a challenge window. A new identity starts with no reputation, so an attacker cannot gain weight merely by minting accounts; it must repeatedly do useful work and risk losing its stake when a beacon exposes fraud. Sybils can still collude, but independent checks make their coordination costly: one false claim can trigger a ripple of audits across linked tasks, while honest agents need not trust a single canyon-crossing authority.
